title: Detect a cycle in a linked list
summary: A tortoise walks one carriage at a time and a hare runs two; if the track loops, the hare laps the tortoise and they meet.
goal: Decide whether the track loops back on itself

examples.label: Loops back to the second
examples.explanation: The last carriage links back to the carriage at position 1.

examples.label: Loops to the start
examples.explanation: The second carriage links back to the first.

examples.label: No loop
examples.explanation: The single carriage links to nothing.

ladder.name: Remember every carriage visited
ladder.idea: Walk the track, keeping a set of carriages seen. Seeing one twice means a loop; reaching the end means none.

ladder.name: Tortoise and hare
ladder.idea: Move one pointer one step and another two steps. If they ever meet, there is a loop; if the fast one reaches the end, there is none.
ladder.insight: Inside a loop, the hare gains one carriage on the tortoise every step, so it must land on it. No memory of visited carriages is needed.

transfer.problem: Repeatedly replace a number by the sum of the squares of its digits. Does it ever reach 1, or loop forever?
transfer.explanation: The numbers form a chain where each points to the next; detect a loop with a slow and a fast walker.

selfCheck: Compares nodes by identity, not value.
Checks fast and fast.next before the double step.
Returns False when the fast pointer reaches the end.
